title: Your CAP model needs a service
audience: Full-stack developers new to SAP CAP

environment.description: Local development prototype; @sap/cds 10.1.1, @cap-js/sqlite 3.1.2, Node.js 22+ with node:sqlite. No SAP cloud account required.
prerequisites: Install Node.js 22.13+ (22 LTS recommended) and npm.
Run npm ci at the repository root before recording.
Use the checked-in inventory project; keep installation outside the video.

sources.title: SAP CAP: Using SQLite for Development

claims.text: A service projection exposes Products through an OData V4 endpoint.
The in-memory SQLite demo loads three products from checked-in CSV data.
The demonstrated stock filter returns the two products that have stock above zero.
The service is read-only and rejects the demonstrated create request.

scenes.narration: Your data model isn't an API.
A CAP entity describes data. Add an explicit service projection to expose it. Start with this prepared inventory project.
First, define Products with an ID, title, and stock count. Three rows of sample data are already in the project.
Next, expose that entity through InventoryService. This explicit service definition creates the API. The read-only annotation keeps this example focused on queries.
Run npm run demo. Open this local Products URL, then filter for stock above zero. You get our keyboard and dock.

visual.label: Run the demo, then open the URL

scenes.narration: You have a local OData version four endpoint with real sample results. This is a development prototype; deployment and authentication come later.
Grab the working project and its checks from the repository. Which entity would you expose first?

publication.text:
A data model alone does not expose an API in SAP CAP. Add an explicit service projection.

This local example defines Products, exposes a read-only InventoryService, and queries an in-memory SQLite database seeded from CSV. Its checks exercise OData metadata, seeded results, stock filtering, a missing product, and rejected writes.

The setup is a development prototype. Authentication and deployment are separate steps.
